chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: How the film 'St. Louis Blues' was retitled and later aired
summary: The film was later retitled, and a friend saw her on the late late show under her own name.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So, we sort of got over that little problem easily enough. As I said before, that was a make-it-as-you-go picture, because they actually my part. They created a scene -- I guess it was a scene just to link other scenes together where I was sitting alone, and there was the Nat King Cole Group behind me, and Hoagy Carmichael wrote "Feeling Kind Of Lonesome" for the picture, so I would have some more to do out there. And, of course, by the end of the picture, "St. Louis Blues" was the finale more or less. By this time, I was dressed up and they had the Hall Johnson Choir and a million people, you know. The big finish. But they've shown that movie on late late shows several times. They changed the title.
Because there was a later St. Louis Blues, if you recall, with Lena Horne and Nat King Cole and --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yeah. No. I think -- well, yes. No. Pearl Bailey -- I don't think Billy was in that.
But they changed the title to the other St. Louis Blues to Birth of the Blues. -- No, Best of the Blues.

And, of course, when they were showing it on the late late show, it was cut. But in 1969 when I started back -- you know, I went in to the Riverboat with Bobby Hackett -- they played the full length through the end.
And they also had it billed with the cast and my name was there. So my daughter called me -- she was about twenty-something years old at the time -- and she called --
They showed it about three o'clock in the morning. But she knew it was going to be on. She stayed up until three o'clock.
She called me and said, 'You know you're on the movie?'
I said, 'I know it, I'm looking.'
So they showed it the full length. And
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
all the things I did in it was shown. And she says, "Do you realize this is the first time I ever saw you when you were young?" The picture was made six years before she was born.
So that was classic. But they show it every once-in-a-while, but now the title is "The Best of the Blues."
